newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle post closing gains.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle post closing gains.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed higher on a combination of strong cash cattle ideas and technicals while feeder cattle followed, with gains in that pit forging past early pressure from higher corn futures, traders said.

Concerns that cash cattle prices may be topping gave way to commercial buying in August late while fund technical buying supported back months as prices held chart points and pointed higher, traders said.

"It just seems like, at the retail level, that we are moving meat period, both beef and pork and that's what is keeping the big support under the cattle right now," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities Inc.
Live cattle closed 0.525 to 0.125 cent per lb higher with August up 0.300 at 67.825 cents. Feeder cattle rose 0.550 to 0.150 with August up 0.275 at 81.625 cents.
Boxed beef values have recently risen to their highest levels since early December and some traders believe beef exports are up, possibly to Japan.
"The highest probability is the Japanese -- they are down on meat supplies" in general, Roose added.
Technical support reinforced gains in back months. Fund-based buying was encouraged by the recent chart action which pointed to weekly charts set to break out on the upside, sources said.

RBH notably bought August, October and December live cattle futures on the late advance with buy stops adding to gains, traders said. R.J. O'Brien and RBH had sold August early. Options trades sold August late to keep the price under 68.000 cents. In live cattle options, there was late liquiation of August 68 calls and commission houses sold October 71 and 72 calls, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle futures were pressured much of the day by rising corn futures but were swept higher late on spillover support from live cattle futures, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.08 at $82.46 per cwt, the highest level since March 1994.

Saul Stone bought August late while ADM Investor Services notably bought August and September early, traders said. E.D.& F. Man, LFG and FIMAT Futures USA sold August early. Cargill Investor Services lightly spread long June live cattle/short January feeders, pit sources added.

Boneless beef futures ended mostly lower and trimmings futures mostly higher. Hedger interest weighed on boneless early before Rosenthal bought August up to resistance at 102.00 cents, floor sources said. They also bought August and October trimmings while Lind-Waldock sold late.
Trimmings futures came up to the cash level but overhead resistance was developing on expectations that trimmings will be under pressure next week, traders said.
Boneless beef futures closed 1.00 cent a lb lower to 0.50 higher with August off 0.30 at 102.00 cents. Trimmings ended 0.10 lower to 1.00 higher with August up 0.20 at 46.80 cents.
